description: qou-pdix route 5 / qou-cds1 branch 3. Bring's curve does have a naturally associated elliptic curve -- Serre, y^2 = x^3 - 675x - 79650, j = -25/2 (re-derived here from the equation), Jacobian isogenous to E^4 diagonalising to (5tau,5tau,5tau,tau), per Riera-Rodriguez 1992 held in the library. It is the FIRST candidate source of imaginarity that passes tier-0 D0 in principle, because a flat unitary connection on a torus has U(1)xU(1) monodromy, elliptic by construction -- unlike Im(q), refuted in Step 19. BUT it supplies no phase: j = -25/2 is not a CM invariant (CM j are rational integers), so E has no complex multiplication and tau no closed form; Re(tau) = 1/2 exactly, so the natural angle 2*pi*Re(tau) = pi is a sign; and none of four pre-declared comparisons lands of theta_required = 0.0565947 (ratios 55.5, 277.6, 27.8, 0.0501; closest a factor of 19.94). Direction not refuted -- a KZB construction on E is untouched -- but this curve at face value hands the ladder nothing. Lean: QOU/QBeta/BringEllipticCurveJInvariant.lean, 3 theorems, sorry-free.

assertions.name: serre_j_invariant_is_minus_25_over_2
assertions.detail: j re-derived from y^2 = x^3 - 675x - 79650 as -12.5, matching the library's -25/2 — the transcription is checked, not trusted (Lean bring_serre_j_invariant)

assertions.name: serre_curve_has_no_complex_multiplication
assertions.detail: -25/2 is not a rational integer, so not a CM j-invariant; E has no CM, tau has no closed form, and the curve supplies no DERIVED phase — which was the point of 'naturally associated' (Lean not_cm_j_invariant)

assertions.name: tau_has_real_part_one_half_so_the_angle_is_a_sign
assertions.detail: Re(tau) = 1/2 exactly (forced by j real and negative), so 2*pi*Re(tau) = pi — a sign, not a tunable phase

assertions.name: no_declared_phase_lands_near_the_required_one
assertions.detail: closest of the four pre-declared comparisons misses by a factor of 19.9409 — an order of magnitude; ratios 55.5103, 277.552, 27.7552, 0.0501481. No search was run over combinations, and the threshold is an order of magnitude rather than the factor of 20 a first draft used, which the data missed by 0.06

assertions.name: an_elliptic_curve_is_the_right_KIND_of_source
assertions.detail: a flat UNITARY connection on a torus has monodromy in U(1)xU(1), elliptic by construction — so unlike Im(q) (Step 19) this passes D0 in principle. Structural, not measured; recorded as the reason the direction stays open

parameters.source: library/pjm-v154-n1-p09-s — Riera & Rodriguez, The period matrix of Bring's curve, Pacific J. Math. 154 (1992) 179-200
parameters.anti_fit: the four comparisons were declared before computing and are reported in full including the misses; no search over combinations was run

context.axis: branch 3: can Bring's associated elliptic curve supply the generator?
context.answer: The right KIND of object -- first candidate to pass D0 in principle, since a flat unitary connection on a torus has elliptic monodromy by construction. But this curve supplies no phase: non-CM, so tau has no closed form; Re(tau) = 1/2 so the natural angle is pi, a sign; and nothing declared lands within a factor of 20.
context.not_refuted: the DIRECTION. A KZB construction on E -- the elliptic analogue of KZ, where exp(2 pi i tau) factors genuinely enter -- is untouched, and is where an elliptic generator could still come from.
context.provenance_caveat: the library copy is OCR of a scanned page and is garbled in places. Only the legible and independently checkable parts are used: the curve equation, its j (re-derived), and the (5tau,...,tau) diagonalisation. The paper's own tau_0 is pinned by TWO j-values, the second illegible in this scan, so tau_0 is NOT reconstructed -- only the SL(2,Z) representative with j = -25/2.
context.scope: Scope-(a). Nothing derived, proposed, wired or readmitted; E is not adopted; no convention adjudicated.
